notes: Title and text say "Mudik Lebaran" while the facts are about Tet (Lunar New Year) travel; this holiday framing is not in the facts.
"Apa pun pilihannya, risiko terbesar justru pakan berlebih": the facts name sitter overfeeding as the main risk, not overfeeding in general for every option.
"Orang yang belum kenal akuarium memang sering kebanyakan memberi pakan": this is supported, but the guide presents it as a general claim.
"Kalau bisa, minta seseorang mengecek feeder setiap beberapa hari": this is supported, but the guide places it in the feeder steps in a slightly different way.
"Tetra, rasbora, guppy, dan corydoras": "Tetra" is read as the fish group, but the facts also name Tetra the brand elsewhere. This is only a minor ambiguity.
The guide adds the "Ganti air dan bersihkan filter" step as a grouped item and tells the reader to "Buang daun tanaman yang mati". The facts support this.
"Untuk lebih dari seminggu, semua sepakat ikan jangan dibiarkan tanpa pakan" - overstated consensus; only one source says not to leave unfed on trips over a week.
"Takar pakan per hari di kotak obat mingguan" - facts say only a pill box with pre-measured daily food; "weekly" is added.
"Pakan beku lebih cocok diberikan oleh orang yang dititipi, ditakar per kubus" - the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion; this is partly an inference.
"Namanya mesin, bisa saja macet" - the facts only say test it because it is a machine; "jam" is an added claim.
"Pakan berlebih jauh lebih berbahaya daripada ikan yang terlewat makan" - the facts say overfeeding by helpers kills more fish, which the guide generalises to all overfeeding.
"Nyalakan lagi filter ... cek sekali lagi bahwa filternya benar-benar jalan" - the facts do not say to double-check this.
"Kalau tetap ingin memakainya, uji dulu seminggu sebelum berangkat" - the facts support testing about 1 week before leaving, but only as a general step.
Minor: "lalu atur lubang rak agar tetesan air merata" and the intro framing are generalizations, but they are consistent with the facts.
Minor: "Pada salah satu rancangan... kapas filter ditaruh di laci pertama" is supported, but "tepat di atas batu aerasi" and "yang dijalankan pompa udara baterai" slightly combine separate facts.
Minor: the FAQ answer "Tetap perlu" for water changes is an inference, but it is supported by the nitrate fact.
"Itulah siklus nitrogen" is not in the facts (minor generalisation).
"Siapkan waktu untuk mencoba dan menyesuaikan" / "perlu dicoba dan disesuaikan" is advice not in the facts.
"Air yang menetes lewat bioball juga mendapat banyak oksigen" overstates the source, which says only that the water becomes well aerated.
"Pasang pompa udara bertenaga baterai secepatnya" adds urgency that the facts do not give.

"Prinsip kerjanya sama-sama wet/dry" in the FAQ presents the keepers' opinion as fact. The "Biasanya karena jumlah lubang..." answer also presents a cause as the usual one, which the facts do not say.
"Akuarium yang ikannya sedikit lebih tahan" is only loosely supported. The facts say lightly stocked tanks cope better after a long outage, so this one is fine.

"Biasanya penyebabnya cahaya berlebih (terutama sinar matahari langsung), pakan berlebih, atau nutrisi berlebih" – the facts list causes but do not say which is usual or most common; minor generalisation.

"Ledakan alga... kematian massal alga bisa ... menaikkan amonia" in the 'Kapan harus khawatir' section – the facts link ammonia spikes to blackout and UV die-off, not to a natural die-off with a colour change; mild extension.

"sterilisator kecil biasanya sudah cukup" is supported, but the claim "Ganti air besar tetap perlu" as a general requirement is a slight extension of the facts, which only call for it after treatment.
"memakai pupuk cair secara umum" – the facts name liquid fertilizer as a cause, so this is roughly supported, but it is phrased more broadly than the source.
"Anggapan ... adalah mitos" – supported by the myths section; no issue.
"kehabisan mineral mikro atau nutrisi kemungkinan merupakan penyebab paling umum" – supported as a hedge, though placed under 'what to do now'.
"Ledakan alga besar paling sering mati karena kehabisan mineral mikro" – the facts say "probably the most common reason"; the guide states it more firmly.
"Inilah bedanya dengan alga yang tumbuh di permukaan" – this contrast is a mild elaboration beyond the facts.
"Tanda alga mati massal" for the sudden colour change – the facts only say the colour usually changes after a die-off, not that it is a warning sign. This is minor.
"menjelang pagi" for the oxygen low – the facts say overnight, so this is a slight specification.
"Bilas sampai tidak ada sisa cuka sama sekali" is supported, but the guide's first vinegar step says to remove fish first only in the limescale section; this is fine.
"Goresan paling sering muncul karena kerikil..." – facts say "common causes", not "most often"; small overstatement.
"Bersihkan lumut dengan pembersih magnet atau pengerik yang cocok untuk kaca atau akrilik, lunakkan kerak kapur dengan cuka putih" – the summary is a generalization not directly in the facts.
"Cara umum: amplas dulu, lalu pakai cairan poles plastik" – facts say sand then plastic polish; ok.
"Silet yang tumpul justru menggores kaca. Ganti bilahnya begitu terasa mulai tersendat" – matches the facts.
Vinegar-strength note: the guide frames it as a source disagreement; reasonable but the claim that "keduanya sepakat" is the guide's own inference.

FAQ: "Pembuat Micro-Mesh ... tetap menyarankan keduanya dikeluarkan" is fine, but "Ada juga sumber yang menyarankan goresan dalam dibiarkan saja" – facts say a scratch on the inside, not specifically a deep one; slight distortion.
"Pakai pengerik plastik, kartu kredit..." in the FAQ is supported.
"usapkan kuku melintang di atas goresan" - the facts only say the fingernail test; the 'across the scratch' detail is unsupported.
"Pakai pembersih magnet... Pertama, cek dulu panel Anda kaca atau akrilik" - generic advice; the facts do not say to check this first.
"untuk kerak kapur pakai cuka putih dengan hati-hati di sisi luar" - the facts do not say to use vinegar only on the outside.

"Kalau akan membersihkan kerak kapur dengan cuka di bagian yang terkena air, keluarkan dulu ikannya" - this adds the condition 'on parts that touch water'. The facts just say to take the fish out first.

"Mulai dari yang paling ringan dan masih efektif" and the numbered polish are fine. However, "Pengerik berbilah stainless steel dan silet khusus kaca tidak cocok" merges the Tetra and ADA facts without naming them; this is a minor point.
"Kalau air keran Anda mengandung kloramin..." - the chloramine point is not tied to cleaning glass in the facts; it is off-topic padding.
"Kerak putih di garis air itu apa, dan berbahaya tidak?" - the facts never say whether limescale is dangerous. The answer implies it is harmless or not, with no support.
"karbon atau media penjerap seumpamanya dikeluarkan": facts say carbon or Purigen; "media penjerap seumpamanya" is a generalisation of Purigen.
"ikan yang dijangkiti perlu dipindahkan ke tangki rawatan" for columnaris: the facts say hospital tank, which is close, but the guide ties it to fin rot in a way the facts don't state.

"ikan laga kerap terkena reput sirip kerana keadaan di kedai ikan hiasan tidak disokong oleh rujukan": the facts only say the claim lacks a citation (Wikipedia). The guide's wording is slightly loose.

"Kanamycin ... boleh dicampurkan ke dalam makanan ... ikut sukatan dan bahan campuran dalam arahan pengeluar": the facts give the mix of 1 scoop KanaPlex, 1 scoop Focus and 1 tbsp food, but the guide leaves it out. This is an omission, not an invented claim.
"Reput ... biasanya oleh bakteria" in the intro: broadly supported, but "biasanya" is a mild generalisation.
"Bakteria ini biasanya memang hidup di dalam air atau dalam lendir kulit ikan" merges two sources; acceptable but slightly blended.
"Asingkan ikan yang suka menggigit atau bergaduh" in step 2: the facts say remove nippers, so this is fine. The facts do not say to isolate fighting fish in this step.
"Pemakanan yang tidak baik dan makanan berlebihan" lists overfeeding as a predisposing factor. The facts name overfeeding as a stressor, so this is a minor generalisation.
"Ubat hanya digunakan jika ikan tidak pulih ... atau jika jangkitan semakin teruk" in the intro: the facts give no 'if the infection worsens' criterion.
"Pandangan sumber berbeza" is the guide's framing, not a fact. It is mild.

"Ubat ini juga boleh dicampur ke dalam makanan ... sehingga 1 minggu": the facts give the recipe (1 scoop KanaPlex, 1 scoop Focus, 1 tbsp food). The guide leaves out the Focus part, but nothing in it is invented.
"Bila perlu risau" bullet 'Reput sudah sampai ke pangkal sirip' as a worry trigger is the guide's own inference. The facts only say tissue cannot regrow.
"Jika mulut ikan turut reput, mungkin itu penyakit columnaris" is a mild extrapolation from the facts. The facts only say columnaris is highly contagious and fish should go to a hospital tank.
"Sumber yang sama mencadangkan suhu air 26–27 °C dan pH 7–8" says 'same source' about the second source (Mytour). This is correct, but 'sumber yang sama' reads ambiguously.

"Penternak menggunakan suplemen mineral untuk mengelakkannya" - the facts only name Wonder Shell/Seachem Equilibrium as skipped minerals. The guide generalizes without naming them, and the claim about what keepers do is slightly beyond the facts.
"Asingkan betina sebelum dia hampir bersalin" in the intro presents separation as a firm rule. The facts say sources differ, and one suggests a divider instead of moving her.

"Jika perut membengkak tetapi gravid spot tidak kelihatan, kemungkinan itu dropsy atau masalah pundi renang" - this is an inference. The facts only say the gravid spot is the key way to tell them apart, not that a missing spot means disease.
"Betina yang bunting juga sering mengejar jantan" is supported. The "Bila perlu risau" heading is the guide's own framing, and the facts don't say when to worry.
"Tangki kira-kira 38 liter": facts say about 10 gallons; the liter conversion is not in the facts (though it is roughly right).
"Jadi betina yang sudah diasingkan daripada jantan masih boleh bunting lagi": this is an inference the facts don't state.
"Jika kandungan lewat melebihi jangka biasa, periksa kualiti air": the facts only say poor water can delay birth. They don't give this advice for an overdue pregnancy.
"Pastikan keadaan airnya sama seperti tangki utama": the facts say this for the nursery tank. The guide moves it into the birthing setup, which is a minor shift.
"Gunakan penapis yang perlahan": the facts say 'gentle filtration'. The 'penapis span' example comes from the colony-breeding source.
"Jika perut besar dan tompok ... semakin gelap ... kemungkinan besar ikan itu bunting": this is a mild generalisation, but it is consistent with the facts.
"suplemen mineral untuk akuarium": the facts name Wonder Shell and Seachem Equilibrium. The guide generalises them, which is acceptable.
"Untuk ikan omnivor seperti ikan emas" in the intro is a small generalisation; the facts say peas suit omnivores but do not call goldfish omnivores.
"serangga air kecil" for the betta live food: the facts say "water bugs", which is close, but "daphnia (bo bo)" and the rest match. This is a minor loose translation.
"Kekalkan suhu air ikan emas di atas lebih kurang 70°F" is supported, but the earlier advice "Naikkan suhu secara perlahan" in the summary is only loosely backed.
"Ikan selalunya mengambil masa beberapa jam untuk pulih" is worded as general fish recovery. The facts tie this only to a shock-like presentation.
"jeli petroleum" for Vaseline is fine, but the guide gives no context for the advice beyond "bahagian badan yang terkeluar dari air".
"Antibiotik berasaskan kanamycin atau minocycline" – facts only name KanaPlex or Maracyn 2; the active ingredients are not in the facts.
"sisik menegak" – facts say "raised scales"; the wording is close, but "ikan emas/serangga air" detail is fine. Minor.
"Ikan selalunya pulih dalam beberapa jam" – facts say recovery from shock often takes a few hours; stated as a general outcome.

"(kira-kira 19 liter)" for 5 gallons and "kira-kira 26–27°C", "kira-kira 21°C", "5°C" – conversions not in facts (approximately correct, but added). The 5-gallon conversion is slightly off (about 19 L is right for US gallons).
"Biarkan air hanya beberapa sentimeter" – facts say a few inches; unit changed to centimetres, which understates the depth.
"kutu air" for daphnia (bo bo) and "serangga air" for water bugs – loose translations.
"Tempoh puasa... Sumber lain" and "Pastikan kitaran nitrogen tangki sudah lengkap" – paraphrase of "cycle the tank"; acceptable.
FAQ "kalau ramai ikan bertindak pelik, uji air dulu" – an inference not stated in the facts.

"Keracunan ammonia, nitrit atau nitrat... boleh membuatkan ikan berenang tidak terkawal" – facts only list ammonia as a nervous-system look-alike, and nitrate for goldfish. Nitrite is not stated to cause this.
"kira-kira 19 liter" for 5 gallons is a conversion not in the facts (arithmetically fine, but added).
"Langkah pertama... supaya ammonia dan nitrit kembali ke sifar" and "Selepas itu barulah pilih rawatan" is an ordering the facts do not state.
The intro says popeye is "akibat penyakit lain, kecederaan atau jangkitan"; this is a loose paraphrase of the facts.

"Rendaman garam untuk punca parasit ... Dalam tangki berasingan" merges the 1–3% bath with the separate-tank note. The facts list the separate tank for the formalin/salt/malachite green treatments, not for the bath specifically.
"Permukaan luar mata... Mata juga mungkin menunjukkan bintik putih atau merah" is fine, but the source for the bintik is a general fish description, not popeye-specific.
"Ikan emas dan cichlid besar ... menghasilkan banyak kotoran" is fine, but the guide says "popeye biasanya akibat penyakit... bukannya penyakit yang berdiri sendiri", which adds emphasis.

"Popeye pada kedua-dua mata lebih cenderung ke arah masalah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman" - the facts do not say bilateral popeye points to water quality or internal disease. This is an invented diagnostic rule, repeated in the FAQ.

"Popeye pada sebelah mata sahaja mungkin berpunca daripada kecederaan" - the facts say injury may cause one-eye popeye. The guide extends this into a diagnostic rule and adds "digigit ikan lain" in the FAQ, which is slightly beyond the facts.
"Jika kedua-dua mata terkena, atau ikan juga berperut buncit... punca yang lebih mungkin ialah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman seperti dropsy" - an unsupported inference.
"tuberkulosis ikan" and "penyakit buah pinggang" are slight embellishments. The facts say only "tuberculosis" and "kidney disease".
"Ichthyophthirius multifiliis (penyakit bintik putih)" - the white spot disease label is not in the facts.
"kerana itu tandanya masalah dalaman yang lebih serius" (dropsy) - not stated in the facts.
"Sebab itu ikan yang sakit perlu diasingkan" - an extra rationale that the facts do not state for this point.
"supaya ikan tidak panik dan melanggar dinding tangki" - the facts say only that the fish should not panic and crash. Reading it as hitting the tank walls is a minor addition.
"Sebab itulah luka cetek ... boleh membawa maut" links the enzyme secretion to fatality; the facts do not state this causal link.
"Jangkitan yang berulang boleh berkait dengan rawatan berlebihan" is a slight stretch. The facts say overtreatment can lead to recurring infections, but this is presented as a reason for concern.
"Sesetengah sumber menegaskan" is vague. The facts attribute the claim to Practical Fishkeeping only.
"Columnaris dirawat dengan antibakteria seperti acriflavine" omits Terramycin. This is not an error.
"Kulat ini tidak boleh dihapuskan sepenuhnya" is supported.
"Dos berbeza mengikut sumber" and the table's "Satu sumber" labels are generalisations, but they are broadly consistent with the facts.
"Garam bukan beriodin" (non-iodised salt) is not in the facts.

"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada 0–35 °C (32–95 °F) tetapi paling suka 15–30 °C": the Celsius conversions are not in the facts, which give only °F. The facts' 32–95°F is about 0–35°C and 59–86°F is about 15–30°C, so the numbers are right but the Celsius values are added.
"Walaupun begitu, kebanyakan penghobi tetap memanggilnya kulat": the claim about hobbyists is not in the facts.

"Cari punca asal seperti ... suhu terlalu rendah" and "Buang bahan organik yang mereput dan telur yang mati" are placed in the immediate-action list. The facts support them as causes and prevention, but not as first-aid steps.
"Perlu tutup penapis karbon semasa rawatan? Ya.": the facts say only that carbon removes medication. They do not say to switch it off, although this is a reasonable inference.

"Lebih membimbangkan lagi jika jangkitan berulang, kerana ia tanda punca asal belum diatasi atau rawatan diberi berlebihan": this interpretation of recurrence is partly invented. The facts link recurrence only to overtreatment.
"Pastikan dahulu ia bukan columnaris" and "atau ada tanda parasit luaran" as a reason to worry are framed as advice not found in the facts.
Table row 'Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg' omits the fact that the dose is 35–125 mg/kg in food; this matches, but 'Sumber 3' attribution is fine. No issue.
'Rendaman dalam tangki' row: facts only say 'bath' (24 hours); 'dalam tangki' is a slight embellishment.
'membiak dengan cepat dalam sistem tertutup seperti akuarium': 'seperti akuarium' is an added example not in the facts.
'Sesetengah produk ubat cacing komersial dilaporkan boleh membahayakan siput': the facts say specifically 'Dactycid can harm snails'. Generalising to commercial products is a slight distortion.
'Kenal pasti kumpulannya kalau boleh': the facts say to work out which family is present, without the 'if possible' hedge. Minor.
'Satu sumber mengulang dos 2.5 mg/L pada hari ke-7 dan ke-14' and 'Penyelidik mencadangkan': minor rewording, supported.

'Ambil perhatian serius jika ikan ... mula mati' and the 'bila perlu risau' section are guide-framed advice assembled from the facts rather than stated in them. This is a small unsupported generality.
'Kurangkan makanan' in the immediate steps is not stated in the facts. The facts only say overfeeding raises ammonia.

Table: "Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg selama sehingga 3 hari" is fine, but the intro claims "menyebabkan ikan ... insang membengkak" as a general sign; swelling is only in severe cases (minor generalisation).

"Kes yang berat boleh merebak dengan cepat dalam tangki, terutamanya pada suhu 22–25°C": the facts only say development is fast at that temperature; the claim about severe cases spreading is a stretch.
"Dapatkan bantuan doktor haiwan akuatik untuk pemeriksaan mikroskop dan preskripsi ubat": the vet is mentioned only for prescribing praziquantel in the US; this broader advice is not supported.
"Celup garam (garam tanpa iodin)": the facts do not mention iodine-free salt.
"hanya dalam tangki hospital yang beroksigen tinggi": the facts say well-aerated, not high-oxygen (minor).
"Praziquantel ... ubat pilihan utama ... Kalau cacing insang disahkan" in the intro: no problem, but "Ulang dos mengikut jadual" is generic.
FAQ: "keberkesanan celup garam berbeza mengikut spesies cacing": roughly supported by the Gyrodactylus data, but it is generalised.
"Satu produk ubat cacing insang komersial ... baca label dengan teliti": the facts only name Dactycid as harming snails; the advice to read the label is added.
"Bahan pengikat membantu" is supported. "Kajian ... masing-masing mengurangkan jangkitan lebih daripada 90 peratus" is supported.
"Sampel ... pernafasan makin laju" is supported. The vet advice and the label-reading advice are the main additions.
"Ikan perlu dikuarantin kerana punca dropsy mungkin berjangkit" is supported. The FAQ line "Kuarantin disarankan..." is also supported.
"(kira-kira 19–38 liter)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is roughly correct, but it is an added number.
"(kira-kira 28–30 °C)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is added, and 82–86°F is closer to 28–30°C, so it is acceptable but unsupported.
"(kira-kira 13 mg seliter)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is added and unsupported.

"Pada dropsy ... selalunya ada tanda lain seperti mata tersembul, insang pucat atau ikan berhenti makan" is only loosely supported. The facts say tumours lack the other signs of disease, but they don't say "selalunya".
"Sumber-sumber tidak sama pendapat" and the claim that sources disagree on the chance of recovery are a framing the facts don't state. The underlying content is supported.
"Rawat air paip dengan penyahklorin" is supported. The 25–50% twice-weekly water change is attributed to a single source, which is acceptable.
"sirip terlipat rapat ke badan" is a rewording of "clamped fins" and is acceptable.
"Kuarantin paling berkesan jika penyakit dikesan awal" is supported.

"Peluang sembuh paling baik jika dikesan awal" in the intro is a generalisation. The facts only say some fish improve if treated early, and that quarantine works best when the illness is caught early.
"Uji air tangki (ammonia, nitrit, nitrat, pH)" lists specific parameters. The facts only say to test the water.
"ikan ditangkap atau dipindahkan" is a paraphrase of "handling". It is acceptable but loosely worded.
"Perhatikan ikan lain, terutamanya yang sama spesies" as a first-aid step is not stated in the facts.

"Kebanyakan sumber mengatakan ... prognosisnya buruk" and "sumber-sumber agak sepakat" are framing claims. They are roughly supported, but the FAQ line "Bagi ikan kecil ... sering disarankan" overstates the facts, which say the euthanasia advice comes from one source.
The intro says "selalunya kualiti air yang teruk dalam jangka masa panjang dan jangkitan bakteria". This is supported only loosely.
"Sebab itu ikan yang sakit perlu dikuarantin" in the FAQ is a reasonable inference, but it is not directly stated in that form.
"Menurut satu sumber... masing-masing boleh menyebabkan cecair terkumpul dalam rongga perut" is a paraphrase of ascites. It is fine.
"Sumber lain menyebut pemulihan tidak mungkin" is softened from "unlikely" to "not possible" ("tidak mungkin"), which is a slight overstatement.
"sisik menegak seperti pain" (pinecone scales) is in the facts only as a pinecone-scales emergency sign, but the guide's phrasing is acceptable; minor.
"Menaikkan suhu ke hujung atas julat yang sesuai untuk ikan laga" omits the 74-81°F range from the facts; generalised but not wrong.
"Menurut satu sumber veterinar, tiada rawatan untuknya" for Cryptobia is supported (Merck).
"Arowana ... secara semula jadi menjadi kurang aktif dan makan kurang": the facts say 'slow down and eat less', which is close enough.
"Jangan terlalu banyak" and "Selalunya beberapa cara ini perlu digabungkan" are supported.
"Jika ammonia atau nitrit melebihi sifar, tukar air dengan segera" in the intro omits the 30-50% figure and slightly turns a conditional recommendation into an urgent one; minor.
"Pea puffer dan scarlet badis ... memerlukan makanan hidup atau beku" is supported.
"Ikan juvenil ... anak ikan dan ikan juvenil yang tidak makan lebih daripada 24 jam" is supported as an emergency.
"Sembelit ... Jika dibiarkan, sembelit boleh menyebabkan masalah pundi renang" is supported.
"Ikan dewasa sudah melepasi tempoh puasa selamat untuk jenisnya" as a worry trigger is an inference not directly stated in the facts.
"kira-kira 23–27 °C" is an invented Celsius conversion of 74–81°F. The facts give no Celsius figure, and 74–81°F is about 23–27°C.
"Sembelit" is presented as a general treatment. The facts only say that fasting for 24–48 hours can clear constipation. They do not link this to a fish that refuses food.

"Guna blok makanan" is listed as a common mistake. The facts only say that food blocks can leave uneaten food rotting and that many species do not recognise them, so this is a mild over-generalisation.

"Ikan laga baru yang stres ... Ya, ikan baru yang stres ..." and "Beri makanan lama bersama makanan baru" in the FAQ for betta pellets applies the old-with-new advice to this case. The facts give that advice for switching foods in general, so this is a small extension.

"Air yang lebih panas pula meningkatkan metabolisme" and the other general statements are supported. "Patutkah saya terus tukar air..." combines facts about old tank syndrome and water changes. The FAQ answer is a plausible synthesis, but it presents "selalunya melebihi 10 mg/L" as the trigger for avoiding water changes, which the facts do not exactly say.
"Insang dan darah bertukar warna coklat gelap seperti coklat" - facts say chocolate-brown; minor wording, fine.
"(lebih kurang 0.95 liter)" - the litre conversion for one quart is not in the facts (small added detail, correct but unsupported).
"Ikan keli saluran" for channel catfish - translation addition, harmless.

"Kedua-dua keadaan ini memerlukan ikan dipindahkan, bukan sekadar tukar air" - the facts give this for old tank syndrome and for ammonia >5 mg/L with pH <7, but the 'not just water change' wording for the second condition is an extrapolation.
"Ikan yang keracunan nitrit ... Ikan berkumpul dekat saluran udara" listed as a worry sign - fine.
"pemanas cepat menghabiskan bateri" - facts say it drains the battery; 'cepat' is a small embellishment.
"Pertimbangkan diagnosis makmal ... Punca tidak dapat dikenal pasti" - 'when to worry more' advice is not in the facts, but is a reasonable generality.
"Ikan yang hampir mati ... patut dimatikan" - supported.
"tidak lebih daripada kira-kira 0.5 °C sejam" contradicts the facts: the limit is 1°F (about 1°C) per hour.
"kira-kira 1 liter air tangki" is a conversion/change: the facts say about one quart (roughly 0.95 L), so it is approximately fine but not exact.
"Insang dan darah bertukar warna coklat seperti coklat masakan" is a odd rewording of chocolate-brown; minor.
"Ikan keli saluran" etc. is supported; "Kalau pH naik lebih daripada 1 unit" is supported.
"kerana paras oksigen paling rendah pada waktu pagi" is supported.
"Pam udara berbateri" is supported.
"Kematian berterusan walaupun parameter air sudah baik" in the worry section is not in the facts (invented trigger).
"pH jatuh di bawah 6.0 dalam tangki yang lama tidak dibuang airnya" is supported only loosely.
The opening line "kuatkan pengudaraan ... uji air" as the first step is a general recommendation not directly in the facts.
"Metronidazole ialah ubat yang paling kerap disebut" is a mild unsupported generalisation; the facts only list it as the treatment.
"Pilih satu kaedah sahaja dan ikut dengan tepat" is advice not stated in the facts, though it is consistent with the warnings against overdosing.

"kepala dan perut yang kelihatan cengkung" is acceptable (sunken head and belly), but the "Rawat jika ikan enggan makan lebih daripada tiga hari" step is placed under first aid without a source ordering. This is minor.
"Metronidazole disenaraikan ... hanya untuk ikan yang bukan ikan makanan" is supported.
The table labels the 1 g per 20 gallons dose as "Dalam tangki" and the Vietnamese method as "Rendaman". The "rendaman" label for the Vietnamese method is an interpretation of "2-day soak".
"lebih kurang 75 liter" for 20 gallons is an added conversion not in the facts (roughly correct).
"lebih kurang 30–31 °C" and "lebih kurang 35.5 °C" are conversions not in the facts. The facts only imply Fahrenheit for 86–88.
"Hexamita memang punca yang paling terkenal" is supported, but "selalunya dikaitkan dengan Hexamita" in the intro is a mild generalisation.
"Perut membengkak; dalam kes lain kepala dan perut kelihatan cengkung" merges separate keeper accounts. It is acceptable but loosely framed.

"Seorang penternak mencadangkan makanan berubat untuk dua atau tiga kali pemberian setiap tiga bulan" is supported. "Penternak berpengalaman" as the source label for the 1 g/20 gal dose is not in the facts.
"rawat dalam tangki berasingan" in the shrimp/snail FAQ answer is an inference. The facts only say metronidazole is toxic to shrimp and snails.
"Jangkitan pada ikan yang baru dihantar boleh membawa maut dalam masa seminggu" generalises the angelfish shipping finding to discus.
The moderator's "digantikan dengan ubat campuran untuk parasit dalaman" paraphrases API General Cure with extra description.
"แพะ (corydoras)" - corydoras is rendered oddly as 'แพะ' (goat); a translation error, not in the facts.
"อาหารแช่แข็งแบบก้อนเหมาะกับการฝากคนมาให้มากกว่า" - the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion for sitters; the comparison 'more suitable' is a mild generalisation.
"บอกไว้ว่าถ้าวันไหนมาไม่ได้ ให้ข้ามมื้อนั้นไปเลย" - the facts say to skip a missed day; the guide frames it as an instruction to the sitter, which is a reasonable reading.
"ตรวจให้แน่ใจว่าเปิดระบบกรองกลับแล้ว" is placed as a preparation step; the facts list it only as a common mistake, which is a minor reframing.
"ซึ่งทำให้ปลาตายมากกว่าการอดอาหารไปบางมื้อ" - this is supported by one source, but the guide states it in the intro as a general fact.
"ถ้าเลี้ยงปลาที่เลือกกิน หรือต้องไปนานกว่า 1 สัปดาห์" - supported by the facts (picky eaters or trips over a week).
"หนอนแดง ไรทะเล" – frozen food examples (bloodworms, brine shrimp) are not in the facts; the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion.
"ไรแดง" for daphnia – a loose translation; daphnia is a water flea, not exactly 'ไรแดง'. This is a minor wording issue.
"ควรมีคนแวะมาดูเครื่องทุก 2–3 วัน" – the facts say 'check every few days' for the feeder. The 2–3 day interval is specific to sitter visits, so this is a slight specification.

"ถ้าไม่อยู่นานกว่า 1 สัปดาห์ก็ไม่ควรปล่อยให้อดเช่นกัน" is placed right after the large/carnivorous/older fish sentence. The facts do support it as a general rule, so the placement is slightly misleading.
"ภายใน 2–3 วันหลังกลับมา" – the facts say 'within a few days'. The 2–3 figure is a slight specification.
"ที่ทำให้ปลาตายบ่อยที่สุดคือการให้อาหารมากเกินไป" – the facts say overfeeding by helpers kills more fish than missed meals. The intro generalises this to all overfeeding.
"ควรเผื่อเวลาปรับจำนวนรูให้ลงตัว" (allow time to adjust the number of holes) is advice not in the facts.
"ส่วนสิ่งสำคัญคือทำให้น้ำกระจายทั่ววัสดุกรองอย่างสม่ำเสมอ" is a mild generalisation. The facts only say an even trickle is hard.
"ได้รับอากาศดีมาก" (very well aerated) slightly overstates the facts, which say "well aerated".
"เมื่อไฟกลับมาแล้วให้ตรวจดูว่าปั๊มทำงานต่อจริง" narrows the facts. They say to check that the filter restarted, not specifically the pump.
"เพราะปั๊มไม่ต้องดันน้ำขึ้นสูงมาก" – the facts only say one keeper argues it loses less flow to pump head; this reason is invented, and it is also odd because a top-mounted unit pumps water up.
"ถ้าไฟดับ ให้เปิดปั๊มลมแบบใช้แบตเตอรี่ทันที" – the facts only say a battery air pump keeps fish supplied with oxygen; "immediately" is an added instruction.
"จึงควรค่อย ๆ ปรับไป" – the advice to adjust gradually is not in the facts.
"ตามวงจรไนโตรเจน" – the nitrogen cycle is not named in the facts.
"ซัมพ์ที่ใช้ K1 แบบเคลื่อนที่" – the facts say a fluidised-bed K1 sump; this is acceptable but slightly reworded.
"ให้ใส่ไว้ในลิ้นชักที่อยู่ต่อจากใยกรอง" and "ชั้นแรกเป็นกรองกล ตามแบบที่ใช้กันทั่วไป" – these mix two different keepers' designs into one prescriptive installation procedure.
"ส่วนการปล่อยน้ำออกทางสเปรย์บาร์ใกล้ผิวน้ำน่าจะช่วยให้เงียบลง" – the facts only say one keeper expected the spray bar to be quiet; the guide presents this as a general likelihood.
"ระหว่างนี้ให้ย้ายวัสดุกรองชีวภาพ... ตรงเหนือหัวทรายของปั๊มลมแบตเตอรี่" – this is roughly supported, but the facts say the media goes above the airstone, not specifically the battery pump's airstone.
"ถ้าสาหร่ายหนาแน่นมากและการให้อากาศอ่อน" is supported, but "ปลาลอยอยู่ใต้ผิวน้ำ... แสดงว่าออกซิเจนอาจต่ำ" is slightly extended from the facts (minor).
"ผู้เพาะพันธุ์บางคนจึงตั้งใจทำน้ำเขียว" adds the causal "therefore", which the facts do not state (minor).
"แหล่งข้อมูลหนึ่งยังระบุการใส่ปุ๋ยน้ำว่าเป็นสาเหตุหนึ่งด้วย" is supported only loosely by the facts (minor).
"ไม้น้ำจะทรุดโทรม" slightly overstates "hard on plants" (minor).
"หรือใช้ปุ๋ยน้ำอยู่แล้ว" – the facts list liquid fertilizer as a cause, but the guide's wording is a loose addition and is weakly supported.

"จุดนี้ใช้แยกน้ำเขียวออกจากตะไคร่ที่เกาะตามพื้นผิว" – the facts say algae float rather than grow on glass. They don't say this distinguishes green water from other algae, so this is an added inference.
"ให้เพิ่มการให้อากาศทันที" – the facts have no instruction to increase aeration immediately. They only say to keep aeration running.

"น้ำที่เคยเขียวเข้มเปลี่ยนเป็นดำ เทา น้ำตาล หรือใสขึ้นมาเอง แสดงว่าสาหร่ายอาจตายลงจำนวนมาก ... แอมโมเนียอาจพุ่งขึ้น" – this reading is an inference. The facts say the colour change follows a die-off, and say nothing about 'on its own' or about an ammonia warning in this context.

"สาเหตุที่น่าจะพบบ่อยที่สุดคือแร่ธาตุหรือธาตุอาหารในน้ำหมด" – the facts give this as the likely reason a large bloom dies back. The guide places it in the immediate-action section with loose framing, and 'prepare for it' is not a stated recommendation.
"แล้วการเปลี่ยนน้ำตามปกติจะทำให้น้ำใสขึ้น" is supported. "ตู้โชว์" (display tank) in the FAQ is not in the facts, which only say green water hides the view.

"ส่วนใหญ่เกิดจากเม็ดทรายที่ติดแผ่นแม่เหล็ก ... " – the facts list several common causes with no ranking; 'mostly' sand in the pad is not supported. The FAQ repeats it as "ส่วนใหญ่เป็นเพราะมีทรายหรือเศษกรวดติดอยู่".
"ส่องดูกระจกทุกด้าน" – the facts say check the panels regularly under good light. 'Every side' is a mild embellishment.
"ปล่อยไว้แล้วหมุนตู้ ... จะดีกว่าการขัด" is framed as 'some sources'; the facts attribute it to one source (WikiHow).
"ส่วนด้านนอกใช้ได้" – outside use of glass cleaner is supported only if sprayed on a cloth, which the guide states; fine.
"ใช้ใบมีดโลหะ... ที่ขูดที่ใช้ใบมีดสแตนเลสและมีดโกนขูดตู้" – the Tetra GS 45 and ADA Pro Razor product names are dropped and generalised; this is acceptable but not exact.
"เม็ดทรายที่ติดแผ่นแม่เหล็ก ... อุปกรณ์ขัดที่หยาบเกินไป" – 'abrasive tools too coarse' is a loose generalisation of metal scrubbers.
"ขูดตะไคร่ด้านในก่อนเปลี่ยนน้ำ ... ใช้น้ำส้มสายชูขาวกับคราบหินปูนโดยไม่ให้หยดลงตู้ที่มีน้ำ" – the intro is consistent with the facts.

"แหล่งข้อมูลพูดถึงความเข้มข้นไม่ตรงกัน ... ทั้งสองแหล่งตรงกันว่าควรเป็นน้ำส้มสายชูขาว" – the facts only say undiluted white vinegar for stains and diluted white vinegar for cleaning the tank. They don't say both sources agree. The guide infers this.

"หลังขัดด้วยกระดาษทรายแล้ว ให้ขัดเงาต่อด้วยน้ำยาขัดพลาสติก" - the facts say sand then use plastic polish, but only in the context of acrylic tanks; the Micro-Mesh step list itself does not include it. This is a mild stretch.
"ถ้าใช้แม่เหล็กสำหรับกระจกบางกับกระจกหนา แรงดูดจะไม่พอและแม่เหล็กจะหลุดง่าย" - the facts say it grips poorly and slips, which matches closely. This is fine.

"ตรวจกระจกทุกด้านเป็นประจำ" and the "ตรวจหลังทำความสะอาด" section - the post-cleaning checklist (re-check with a fingernail, look for new faint scratches) is the guide's own addition. The facts do not give it as a post-cleaning procedure.
"ถ้ายังสะดุดอยู่แสดงว่ารอยยังลึก" - the fingernail test is applied to a scratch after polishing, which the facts do not say.
"ย้ายปลากลับ" and "ล้างน้ำส้มสายชูออกให้หมดทุกจุดก่อนเติมน้ำ" - the checklist and the general advice to rinse are loosely supported. The extension to polish residue is not in the facts.
"รอยตื้น: ... ถูน้ำยาขัดเบา ๆ เป็นวงกลม" - this matches the facts for glass, so it is fine.

The chloramine bullet in the prevention section is placed there as advice, and the facts do not tie it to cleaning. It is a fact about tap water that has little to do with the topic, so it is tangential but not wrong.
"Mốc 1–3 ngày là mốc an toàn mà nhiều nguồn cùng nêu" is a mild generalization; the sources differ (2–3 days vs 1–3 days).
"Dù chọn mốc nào cũng đừng để dồn tới phút chót" blends the last-minute-rush mistake into the timing advice. This is a small extension.
"Có mẫu máy sục khí chạy pin... 20 tiếng" drops the Aquarium Co-Op attribution. This is minor.
"Bạn nên nhờ người ghé qua kiểm tra máy vài ngày một lần" is fine, but "Người chưa chơi cá thì đừng nhờ cạo rêu" turns the beginner advice into a general one. This is minor.
The sitter step "để người trông châm thêm khi nước bay hơi" adds a purpose the facts do not give. The facts only say to leave buckets of treated water and mark the level.
"Ở tiệm cá Việt Nam có bán hộp chia thức ăn theo ngày" is supported. "Thức ăn đông lạnh dạng viên" is also fine.
In the power-cut steps, "Trước khi cắm điện lại, vệ sinh lọc" is consistent. But "Dùng sủi khí hoặc lọc bio" for 'sponge filter' is an acceptable paraphrase.
"Cho ăn dư mới là thứ làm chết cá nhiều hơn chuyện cá bị lỡ bữa" is supported, but the intro line "cái hại lớn nhất là cho ăn quá nhiều" is a mild generalisation.

"Có nguồn cho rằng cá khỏe mạnh nhịn tới một tuần vẫn được" overstates the facts. They say a trip of one week or less can be unfed (with Aquarium Co-Op's 7-day quarantine as the reason), but the other sources give 1-3 days.
"Đi Tết cả tuần thì lượng nước hụt không nhỏ" is an inference. The facts only give the Singapore figure of 2-3 L a day for a 120 L tank.
"Bể cần ổn định trước khi bạn vắng nhà" and "Máy móc thì có lúc trục trặc" are paraphrase-level additions, not in the facts.
"Lá mục để lại trong bể sẽ làm amoniac tăng" is roughly supported (dead leaves could raise ammonia). The advice to check by eye that the filter is running is an invented addition.
"bám trên lũa, đá và lá cây" for the biofilm is an unsupported detail.
"Có nguồn khuyên đặt 6–8 tiếng" is supported. "Máy tốt phải giữ thức ăn tránh ánh sáng" is a slight reframing of the facts.
The FAQ line "Đi 4–7 ngày thì nên dùng máy ... với thức ăn khô" is supported by the facts, though the pairing is a synthesis.
The FAQ says slow-dissolving blocks "gây rêu, đục nước và tăng pH" as if one source said all of it. This merges two different sources.
"Bể dài tối đa" column: facts say 'tanks up to 40/50/60 cm', not specifically tank length; small reinterpretation.
"Số ngăn ... Không ghi" for G60: acceptable, not a claim.
"vì bơm không phải đẩy nước lên cao nhiều": facts only say less flow lost to pump head; 'không phải đẩy nước lên cao nhiều' is a slight embellishment.
"Bạn cần chạy sủi bằng pin càng sớm càng tốt": urgency is not in facts, which only say bacteria begin dying after about an hour.
"Lấy vật liệu vi sinh ... đặt vào bể ngay phía trên quả sủi": facts say 'may keep bacteria alive', fine; but the FAQ answer implies this as a recommendation more firmly.
"Khay ít lỗ quá: nước không thoát kịp": the mechanism is a mild elaboration of the overflow fact.
"Thả cá quá sớm" listed under common mistakes: the facts mention this risk but not under tray mistakes; minor.
"Dân chơi gọi... loại đặt dưới gầm bể": 'under the tank' for lọc tràn dưới is inferred from sump facts; mild.
"Mất điện là chuyện thường gặp ở mình" is not in the facts.
"Lớp này giữ cặn để cặn không chui xuống các tầng sau" gives a purpose for the pre-filter that the facts do not state.
"Nước chảy thành dòng... bỏ qua phần lớn vật liệu" adds a detail beyond the facts, which only mention channeling being hard to avoid.
"bạn đừng nản nếu phải chỉnh vài lần" is an invented reassurance.
"Cách này nhiều khả năng giữ được vi sinh sống" strengthens the facts, which say only that it "may keep" the bacteria alive.
"Bông lọc để ở ngăn đầu tiên... mỗi lớp dày khoảng 2 inch" generalises the 2-inch depth to every layer. The facts give it only for the polyester floss in the pre-filter tray.
"Cho nước về qua thanh phun sát mặt nước cũng là một cách để lọc chạy êm hơn" presents as fact something the keeper only expected to be quiet.
"lọc tràn trên ngừng ngay khi bơm tắt" is not in the facts.
"Xem nước có rải đều không" is listed as a check item, but the facts do not give it as a post-outage or maintenance check.
"Ở Việt Nam, người chơi lọc tràn trên vẫn quen dùng sứ lọc, đá nham thạch và san hô vụn" turns a list of part names into a claim about common practice.
"Phần lớn trường hợp chỉ cần đi đủ các bước sau" is an unsupported generalization.
"Thay nước nhiều sau khi xử lý để vớt bớt xác tảo" is only roughly supported. The facts say a large water change after treatment removes dead algae and ammonia.
"đây là chỗ phân biệt nước xanh với các loại rêu bám" is an added claim. The facts only say the algae float rather than grow on glass or decor.
"Nhiều người tin thay một lần nước lớn là hết xanh" is a mild embellishment. The facts present it as a myth from one source, Buce Plant.
"đèn bật quá lâu, nắng từ cửa sổ" is listed under the light cause. This is supported, but it is merged with the 'too much light' cause.
"bộ chỉnh độ sáng" is a rendering of 'dimmer'. It is fine.
"lờ đờ không phản ứng khi bị động" adds 'lờ đờ' (lethargic), which the facts do not mention. The facts say only that fish gulp air and ignore disturbances.
"Mùa nóng thì nguy cơ này cao hơn" is applied to the die-off oxygen depletion. The facts link warm water to night-time oxygen loss from a dense bloom, not to the die-off.
"Các cửa hàng cá cảnh ở Việt Nam đều bán đèn UV" - facts say shops sell them; "đều" (all) is an overgeneralization.
"Quan sát cá vào sáng sớm, lúc oxy trong bể thấp nhất" - the facts say fish hang at the surface in the early morning, but they don't say this is when oxygen is lowest.
"Vì vậy, hễ thấy nước đổi màu đột ngột thì bạn phải tăng sủi ngay" - this instruction is not in the facts.

"Tuyệt đối đừng tắt lọc hay sủi" and the mistake "Tắt sủi vào ban đêm trong lúc nước đang xanh đặc" - the facts say to keep aeration running, but they don't list turning it off at night as a common mistake.
"Một bể xanh đặc có thể kéo oxy hòa tan xuống gần bằng không chỉ sau một đêm" - this is a mild embellishment of 'close to zero overnight'.
"Cách này thường dùng kèm với một trong hai cách trên" (fine floss) - the facts don't say it is usually combined with blackout or UV.
"Không đặt bể ở chỗ nắng chiếu thẳng vào" is listed under prevention - the facts give it only as a cause-cutting step, not as a prevention item. This is minor.
"tảo dùng cạn khoáng vi lượng hoặc dinh dưỡng trong nước" - this is close to the facts, but they don't say it directly.
"Thông tin hiện có không cho biết loại bột này chứa gì... Riêng các chất tẩy cặn vôi... chắc chắn độc với cá" is an unsupported framing: the facts only mention the powder, not its safety.
"Vết xước nhẹ thì đánh bóng được" is a mild generalisation not stated in the facts.
"Mặt ngoài thì dùng được" for household glass cleaner is slightly extended. The facts only say to spray it onto the cloth.
"Kem đánh bóng" for light glass scratches is described as polishing compound; this is fine, but the 'rửa sạch' step is slightly extended.
"Thoa kem đánh bóng nhựa" and the acrylic sand-then-polish step are supported, but "Làm xước acrylic" for Scotch-Brite is fine.
The final checklist item "lưỡi dao còn bén không" reverses the facts: a dull blade is what scratches, so the guide's wording is odd but consistent. Minor.
"Rút hết nước" and "bắt cá ra" for inside repairs are phrased as certain; the facts say "may mean".
"Kính bị xước là do lưỡi cùn chứ không phải do lưỡi bén" overstates the fact: a dull blade scratches glass, but nothing says sharp blades don't scratch.
"Móng không vướng thì tự đánh bóng được" is not supported. The facts only say that a nail catching means the scratch is probably too deep.
"Dao cạo lưỡi thép không gỉ, kể cả các loại dao cạo chuyên cho bể cá, chỉ dành cho bể kính" generalises beyond the facts. They cover only the Tetra GS 45 and the ADA Pro Razor.
"Các nguồn hướng dẫn khác nhau ở độ đậm của giấm... Cả hai nguồn đều thống nhất là chỉ dùng giấm trắng" is invented framing. The facts do not say the sources agree.
"Nam châm làm cho kính mỏng mà đem dùng cho kính dày" is a slightly garbled paraphrase and adds nothing supported.
"Lưỡi bắt đầu rít hoặc kéo nặng tay thì thay lưỡi mới" changes "drag" to "rít" and adds "kéo nặng tay". It is minor.

"Để nước qua đêm không làm mất chloramine được" adds "overnight", but the facts say only that leaving the water to stand doesn't remove chloramine. The claim that many places have chloramine in tap water is also not in the facts.
"Cá có thể bị stress... Vì vậy khi tẩy vôi ở mặt trong" is acceptable. "Cặn còn lại có thể làm chết cá" is consistent with the facts.
The "rửa sạch rồi làm lại" and "kem đánh bóng" glass-scratch steps are supported. "Bột tẩy rửa kính bể cá đa năng" is presented without any caveat about whether it is safe.
